# Bosonic Noise Dimension

The project studies ordinary unassisted quantum communication through one-mode iid random Weyl displacements under an unconditional mean input-photon constraint. The noise law is known, the draw is hidden, and its second moment is finite. Its principal theorem identifies capacity up to a logarithmic-logarithmic error from the Shannon entropy of the noise quantized at inverse-square-root energy resolution.

- Arbitrary-block converse, finite-squeezing limit, smoothing/continuity estimates and bounded-capacity criterion: science/03-converse.md.
- Circular displacement noise, exact Skellam entropy and Gaussian covariance comparison: science/04-circular-noise.md.
- Nonzero-jitter achievable rate, saturation and joint energy–broadening limits: science/05-broadening.md.
- Inherited mechanisms and distinctions from prior work: science/06-related-work.md.
- Primary-source identities and exact imported ingredients: references/README.md and references/references.bib.
- Reproducible finite calculations, dependencies and numerical error limits: verification/README.md.
- Conceptual introduction and connected learning route: learning/README.md.
- Common project-defined M01–M30 understanding map, with twelve background and eighteen narrative targets: learning/MILESTONES.md.
- Sole educational anchor, Holevo's second revised and expanded edition (2019), with verified source locations, notation translation and worked example: learning/HOLEVO_BRIDGE.md.

## Scientific distinctions to preserve

The coherent information of the thermal input is an achievable lower bound. Optimality of the leading coefficient requires the separate arbitrary-code converse. Random displacement operators generally do not commute, even though their random-unitary channels compose by classical convolution. Information dimension is neither covariance rank nor support dimension alone.

Zero logarithmic energy slope does not imply a bounded capacity. Finite Gaussian-relative entropy supplies the exact boundedness criterion under the noise-moment hypothesis. Fixed positive Gaussian broadening has a finite ceiling; a vanishing broadening parameter leads to the separately stated crossover. The energy and blocklength limits must follow the specified order.

The proofs do not establish efficient coding, loss robustness, assisted-capacity equality, a universal constant remainder or exact finite-energy Gaussian quantum capacity. The comparison with the phase-noise project credits the shared entropy-resolution principle and keeps the different error algebra, resolution and converse tools explicit.
